meta.title: Pro
meta.description: Several Claude Code accounts with rotation, a request queue, restore points, check on finish and an own folder per session.

hero.title: When the quota runs out, the request waits in the queue and the session switches accounts.
hero.body: Pro adds to Persisty several Claude Code accounts with rotation, the request queue, a restore point on every request, your tests running when the agent stops and an own folder for each session. For {price} a month.

accounts.title: Several Claude Code accounts, no /login in the middle of the day
accounts.body: Connect your personal account and your company's. Persisty follows each one's 5-hour and 7-day windows, sends every new session to the one with the most room and, when a session reaches the limit you chose, moves it to another as its answer ends.
accounts.below: This computer's account, with its live quota.
accounts.here: As many accounts as you have, with rotation and the switch limit you choose.

queue.title: The next request already written, waiting its turn
queue.body: Write it now and choose when it goes: as soon as the agent is free, when the 5-hour window renews or from a chosen time. One at a time, in order, never in the middle of a job or over a permission prompt.
queue.below: You wait for the agent to finish before sending the next one.
queue.here: The queue sends the next one when it can, with Persisty open.

restore-points.title: Take the folder back to before any request
restore-points.body: Each request saves the folder's state before the agent starts. You see what comes back and what would be deleted before you confirm, and restoring keeps the current state as a new point, so you can undo it.
restore-points.below: Points already saved can still be restored.
restore-points.here: A point on every request, up to 50 per session.

verify.title: Your tests run when the agent stops
verify.body: Pick a workspace command, such as pnpm test. When the agent stops after changing files, it runs by itself in the session's folder, and the header says whether it passed, failed or is still running.
verify.below: You remember to run the tests after each request.
verify.here: The result shows in the session header.

worktree.title: Two agents in one repository, never in each other's way
worktree.body: The new session gets a persist/<name> branch in a folder of its own. On closing, Persisty says how many commits the branch keeps and asks whether the folder stays, goes, or goes discarding what was not committed. The branch is never deleted.
worktree.below: A workspace's sessions edit the same folder.
worktree.here: A folder and a branch for each session.

allFree.name: Everything in the free plan
allFree.line: Recovery, projects, agent states, the editor, git, voice, tasks and the network log stay the same.

items.q: Are queued requests sent while Persisty is closed?
items.a: No. The queue is checked every 10 seconds with Persisty open. With the app closed nothing is sent; when you open it again, the queue carries on where it was.

items.q: What happens if I stop paying for Pro?
items.a: Persisty goes back to free. Nothing is lost: saved restore points can still be restored and requests already in the queue still count.

items.q: Do I need internet to use Pro?
items.a: Not all the time. The license is signed and works 14 days offline; the app renews it by itself when there is a connection.

items.q: On how many computers can I use it?
items.a: On up to 5 computers per account. You see and remove each one in My account.

items.q: What currency do I pay in?
items.a: Reais in Brazil and dollars elsewhere. You pay by card, through Stripe, and cancel whenever you like in the subscription portal.

closing.title: Start with the free plan and subscribe when you miss a Pro feature.
closing.body: Persisty's core works without an account. Pro reaches the app by itself as soon as you subscribe.
